title: Gnotobiotic Cockroach Gnotocol
author: Helen Dukes
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.t4ceqsw

steps.title: Collect fresh egg cases
steps.instruction: Pull 3–5 oothecae directly off female abdomens using kimwipes moistened with water or SDS to obtain clean, recently laid eggs.

steps.title: Wash egg cases with SDS
steps.instruction: Place the egg cases in a 5 mL Eppendorf tube containing 1–2 mL of 0.1 % SDS, vortex to wash, then transfer to a new 5 mL tube and repeat the wash once more.

steps.title: Rinse egg cases with sterile water
steps.instruction: Transfer the washed egg cases to a fresh 5 mL Eppendorf tube with 2–3 mL sterile water, vortex to rinse, and repeat rinses in new tubes until no suds remain.

steps.title: Prepare 0.1 % peracetic acid
steps.instruction: Immediately before sterilization, dilute the 32 % peracetic‑acid stock by mixing 10 µL stock with 3.2 mL sterile water to make 0.1 % solution (sufficient for up to 5 oothecae); prepare in a 5 mL Eppendorf or a 15 mL conical tube for larger batches.

steps.title: Acid sterilize egg cases
steps.instruction: Submerge the washed/rinsed oothecae in the 0.1 % peracetic‑acid solution for 5 minutes, inverting occasionally; then move all materials into a sterilized laminar‑flow hood to avoid post‑sterilization contamination.

steps.title: Post‑acid rinse in sterile water
steps.instruction: Using sterile, pre‑autoclaved forceps, transfer each egg case from the acid bath into its own 1 mL of pre‑aliquoted sterile water in a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube, invert repeatedly to rinse, then move the case to a fresh sterile‑water tube for a second rinse (all steps performed in the laminar‑flow hood).

steps.title: Transfer to LB agar slants
steps.instruction: With a new set of sterile forceps, place the rinsed oothecae onto sterile LB‑agar slants inside the laminar‑flow hood, seal the slants in a secondary container, remove the container from the hood, and incubate at 30 °C; hatching should begin after ~4 weeks. Monitor slants daily for microbial growth during the first few days and discard any tubes showing contamination.

steps.title: Maintain and expand nymphs
steps.instruction: Allow newborn nymphs to feed on the LB agar; to prevent dehydration, pipette <1 mL sterile water onto the agar once a week (laminar‑flow hood). Continue monitoring for unwanted microbial growth. When space becomes limited, transfer nymphs to an Erlenmeyer flask containing LB agar at the bottom, performing the transfer in the laminar‑flow hood.
